So there are quite a few different types of key switches. If you're looking for a keyboard, you'll probably have a hard time figuring out what type of switch you want in your new keyboard.

Let's start with cherry mx. The main types of cherry mx switches are Blues - makes a sharp clicking sounds when you've activated the switch. Easy to press. Reds - makes no sound when you've activated the switch. The easiest to press. Browns - makes you go over a small bump in order to activate. Easy to press. Blacks - just like the mx reds, but a little harder to press. No sound during activation or bump. Greens - just like blues, but harder to press. A sharp sound just like blues. Clears - like browns, but harder to press. A nice bump upon activation.

Now for some terms - Linear - no bump or sound upon pressing it down, reds and blacks Clicky - a sound is made upon pressing it down, blues and greens Tactile - a bump occurs upon pressing it down, browns and clears.

Now for some generalizations. And I am talking general. If you like to play fps (first person shooter games, get a linear switch, reds or blacks.) If you want to type a lot at your keyboards, get a clicky switch, blues or greens If you want to type a lot but don't want to make a lot of noise or just want a bump to know when you've hit the switch, get browns or clears. If you have big or really strong hands get the harder to press version of the switch you like.

**A fair warning, these are generalizations, so take it with a grain of salt, also, if you are thinking about getting clears, you will need strong hands, these switches are not for the light harted
